key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Fe-based amorphous coatings achieve better corrosion and wear performance when droplets spread into dense, fine-lamellar structures with fewer porosity defects.
engineering_relevance: Coating process parameters and ambient humidity strongly influence durability, making spray optimization and service-environment control important for steel protection applications.
method: Prepared Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 carbon steel by detonation spray under different spraying parameters.
Evaluated long-term corrosion behavior and tribological performance in different humidity environments.
Related coating microstructure, porosity, and droplet morphology to corrosion resistance and wear behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that circular disk-like droplets with high circularity and expansion factor produced denser coatings, while increased porosity reduced corrosion resistance and higher humidity lowered friction coefficient and wear rate.
watch_item: Performance depends on spray-formed microstructure and environmental humidity, so results may not transfer directly without matching process settings and service conditions.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
